entries.clue: People go through this open entrance (6,9)

blocks.note: read en-TRANCE: to entrance is to enrapture, and a transport is a rapture

annotation.surface: Visitors streaming through an open doorway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway noun; it is the verb or state stressed on the second syllable, meaning rapture, which is a transport of delight.
annotation.definitionFit: Passengers go through public transport on buses and trains every day.

entries.clue: Grounds for pulling up fish on vessels (3,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

annotation.surface: An angler hauling fish up onto boats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pulling up' suggests hauling a line; in the definition it means a driver stopping, and car parks are the grounds for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Car parks are areas of ground where drivers pull up and park.

entries.clue: Perhaps husky fellow’s reply to priest? (4)

blocks.note: 'I do' is the reply to the priest in a wedding service

annotation.surface: A hoarse-voiced man answering a priest, perhaps at his wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Husky' seems to describe the fellow's voice; it is a dog breed, and Fido is a stock name for a dog, so 'perhaps' flags an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Fido is a traditional dog's name, and a husky could be called Fido.

entries.clue: One’s horny wife out of desire to go with lover (8)

indicatorNotes.out of: wife comes out of the word for desire

blocks.note: to elope is to run off with a lover

annotation.surface: A randy wife who longs to run off with her lover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horny' reads as lustful, which fits the whole story; here it means having horns, and an antelope is one such animal.
annotation.definitionFit: An antelope has horns, so it is one that's horny in the literal sense.

entries.clue: Settle bill completely (6)

blocks.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, AD

annotation.surface: Paying off an account in full.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Settle bill' sounds like paying up, but 'settle' is the definition on its own and the bill is a poster.
annotation.definitionFit: To adjust or settle something is to put it right, as in settling a dispute or claim.

entries.clue: Panic had spread around block (8)

indicatorNotes.spread around: the letters are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: Panic spreading through a neighbourhood block.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Block' reads as a building at the end of the surface; it is a verb meaning hinder.
annotation.definitionFit: To handicap someone is to hamper or block their progress.

entries.clue: Naked girl conclusively pinching Romeo’s butt (6)

indicatorNotes.pinching: BARE pinches R, holding it inside

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A naked girl pinching Romeo's backside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butt' looks like a bottom to be pinched; it is a large cask, which is a barrel.
annotation.definitionFit: A butt is a large barrel for wine or beer.

entries.clue: Range that’s largely soothing given treatment (8,7)

indicatorNotes.given treatment: the letters are worked on and rearranged

annotation.surface: A range of therapies that are mostly calming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Largely' looks like it will shorten a word, but it is used whole as fodder; 'range' is a firing range.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the firing sense: a range is any place for target practice, and the fairground booth is one kind.

entries.clue: Uniform policeman’s back dealing supply out (9)

indicatorNotes.back: the back of policeman is its last letter
indicatorNotes.supply: supply as in supple: bend DEALING into a new order

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A uniformed officer going behind the scenes to cut off a dealer's supply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is a noun in the drugs-bust picture; read it as the adverb from supple, meaning flexibly. 'Out' is the definition: out of line.
annotation.definitionFit: Something unaligned is out of line or out of true.

entries.clue: Adult party? Show up (5)

blocks.note: informal British word for a lively celebration

annotation.surface: An invitation to a grown-ups' party, asking guests to turn up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show up' seems to mean arrive at the party; it means embarrass someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: embarrassing someone in public both disconcerts them and exposes them.

entries.clue: Focus for talent: piano picked up with scales (7)

indicatorNotes.Focus for: the focus of a word is its centre
indicatorNotes.picked up: rose means got up, went up

blocks.note: the middle two letters of taLEnt

annotation.surface: A music teacher's note: a gifted pupil's piano playing improved with scale practice.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical scales are the fish-and-reptile kind. Leprose is a rare botanical word for scaly or scurfy.
annotation.definitionFit: Leprose means covered in scales or scurf.

entries.clue: Experience unconscious fit (7)

blocks.note: a go = a fit or bout, as in a coughing go

annotation.surface: Having a fit while unconscious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit' wants to be the definition, as in suitable; it is a noun, a bout, and 'Experience' at the front is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: you go through an operation or a change, which is living through it.

entries.clue: Short, nasty dog needing lead for town (4)

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel or nasty dog

annotation.surface: A small vicious dog that needs a lead to go into town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is a dog's leash in the picture and a first letter in the wordplay; 'Short' is brusque, not small.
annotation.definitionFit: Curt means short in manner, brusque.

entries.clue: Little bit cut off? Career primarily at sea for oil worker (10)

indicatorNotes.cut: BIT is cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.at sea: the letters are all over the place

blocks.note: first letters of Off and Career

annotation.surface: A worker cut off from home by a career at sea on an oil rig.
annotation.walkthrough: The oil rig picture hides a painter: an oil worker is an artist in oils, here Sandro Botticelli, the Renaissance master of The Birth of Venus.
annotation.definitionFit: Botticelli painted in oils, among other media, so he is an oil worker.

entries.clue: Soldiers wait for backup (7)

blocks.note: to wait at table is to serve

annotation.surface: Troops holding on until reinforcements arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wait for backup' reads as one phrase; 'wait' is table service and 'backup' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a substitute player or spare supply kept in hand for when it's needed.

entries.clue: Perform before show and try again endless sex (8)

blocks.note: a court rehears a case when it tries it again

annotation.surface: A bawdy stage direction about repeated sex before curtain-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try again' is legal: a case retried is reheard.
annotation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to perform a piece in practice before the real show.

entries.clue: Bleeding send electronic message to idiot at front (7)

indicatorNotes.at front: the idiot goes before the message

blocks.note: to ping someone is to send them a quick electronic message

annotation.surface: Someone angrily messaging a fool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bleeding' looks like a British expletive, as in 'bleeding idiot'; it means draining.
annotation.definitionFit: Sapping and bleeding both mean draining away strength or resources.

entries.clue: Blinding sun exhausting (8)

annotation.surface: A dazzling sun that wears you out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blinding' seems to describe the sun's glare; it is the British slang for cursing, as in 'effing and blinding'.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: 'effing and blinding' describes cursing out loud, so blinding alone carries the sense of using oaths.

entries.clue: Definitely wearing a suit (2,6)

blocks.note: to be in a suit is to be wearing it
spades is a suit of cards

annotation.surface: Someone sure to be dressed in a suit.
annotation.walkthrough: The suit is a card suit, not clothing.
annotation.definitionFit: In spades means emphatically, to a great degree, definitely.

entries.clue: State of fancy throne surrounding king: gold one (5,5)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: the rearranged THRONE goes round K and OR

blocks.note: THRONE rearranged, split round the middle

annotation.surface: A monarch's ornate golden throne.
annotation.walkthrough: The gilded throne picture suits a regime whose leaders rule like a royal dynasty.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: any sovereign country is a state, and this is one on the Korean peninsula.

entries.clue: Rule over Sweden and abdicate (6)

indicatorNotes.over: REIGN lies over S, covering it

blocks.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

annotation.surface: A Swedish monarch ruling and then giving up the throne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'ruling over Sweden'; in the wordplay it means REIGN lies over S, which sits inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to resign an office, especially a throne.

entries.clue: Just taking in sport in full view (6)

indicatorNotes.taking in: to take in is to admit or house, as a lodger is taken in, so ONLY holds PE within it

annotation.surface: Watching a game in plain sight of everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like it means fair; it is the word ONLY, and PE is the British school-timetable name for sport.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something openly is doing it in full view.

entries.clue: Geographical region like Iowa (4)

blocks.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

annotation.surface: A region resembling the American Midwest.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward America; the region is a continent on the other side of the world.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a continent is the largest kind of region on the map.

entries.clue: Duct with clot blocking side (7)

indicatorNotes.blocking: ASS sits in PAGE, blocking it

blocks.note: a clot is a fool, an ass
a side of paper is a page

annotation.surface: A blood clot blocking a vessel on one side of the body.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical picture makes a clot a lump of blood; it is British slang for an idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: A duct is a passage carrying fluid or air.

entries.clue: American hawk to trade across department (7)

blocks.note: to retail is to trade, to sell

annotation.surface: A US political hawk wanting trade across a government department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' suggests a political hardliner; it is the bird, the red-tailed hawk of North America.
annotation.definitionFit: The redtail is the red-tailed hawk, common across North America.

entries.clue: Blasted right into karate expert (4)

indicatorNotes.into: 'into' means going inside something, so R enters the middle of DAN

blocks.note: a dan is a black-belt grade, and a holder of one

annotation.surface: A karate master blasting someone with a right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blasted' is the mild curse, as in 'that blasted dog', not an attack.
annotation.definitionFit: Darn and blasted are both mild oaths: 'that darn car'.

entries.clue: Fumes from fire ultimately breathed in by kids (5)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: 'ultimately' means in the end, so only the end of 'fire' is used
indicatorNotes.breathed in by: what is breathed in goes inside the breather, so E ends up within RAGS

blocks.note: to rag is to tease or kid, so kids = rags

annotation.surface: Children inhaling smoke from a fire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fumes' is a verb, seethes, and 'kids' is a verb too, teases.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who fumes rages with anger.

entries.clue: You finally ran relay races for a time (5,4)

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' means at the very end, so only the closing letter of 'you' is used
indicatorNotes.races: the letters race about into a new order

annotation.surface: An athlete who ran relay races for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Races' looks like the relay's noun; it is the verb telling the letters to move.
annotation.definitionFit: A lunar year, twelve lunar months, is a period of time.
